transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

...Well. I guess I'm mainly here because HR at work and my sister keep telling me I've gotten too thin. I don't really see it that way. 

My weight has kept dropping since my divorce, but... honestly, from my side, I just see that my suits fit sharper now. So, yeah. That's why I'm here.
Can you describe your eating habits lately? Have you been intentionally limiting how much you eat or avoiding certain types of food?

I guess I just... keep things pretty simple. Most days I just have coffee in the morning. Maybe a protein bar between sales calls if I need it. Then at night, just something small... like some grilled chicken, no rice or anything heavy. 

I don't really like eating more than that because... I don't know. If I actually sit down and eat a full meal, it just feels like I messed up the whole day. So I just stick to what works.
Do you find yourself preoccupied with your body weight or shape, or worry a lot about gaining weight?

I mean... I wouldn't really use the word preoccupied. But... I do pay attention to it. 

Like, if I have a big client dinner, or... if I'm out in Miami for the weekend or something. If I check the scale after and it's even a pound higher, I just... I don't know. I get this sort of panic. It just feels like I'm losing control of things. So I usually just... start planning how to cut back the next day to fix it. Keep it in check. That's all.
After eating more than you plan to, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to avoid gaining weight?
No. I mean... no, I don't do any of that stuff. I don't make myself sick or take pills or whatever. Like I said, I just... I just eat less the next day. That's it.
Would you say that your overall sense of how you’re doing or how you feel about yourself is strongly tied to your weight or how your body looks?

I guess so. Yeah. 

It's just... I don't know. When I'm getting ready, like looking in the mirror before a meeting or... a date or something, I just... I end up staring at my stomach or my face. And if I feel like I look... soft, or whatever... I just think everyone else is going to see that. Like they're going to think I'm sloppy. Or weak. So... yeah, it matters.
Have you lost more weight than you originally intended when you started eating this way?

I don't really know. I didn't... I didn't have a set number in mind when I started or anything. I just wanted to lean out a bit. So... I couldn't really tell you if it's more than I intended. It's just where I'm at now.
Have you ever felt like your body looked different than it actually does, or found yourself misjudging how your weight or shape really looks?
I don't think so. I mean... I see what's in the mirror. It's just... I just see what's there. I don't really know what you mean by misjudging it.
Would you say that your weight or body shape has a strong impact on how you feel about yourself overall?

I mean... I think I just answered that, didn't I? 

But... yeah. Like I said a minute ago, when I'm checking the mirror before a sales pitch or a date... I just zero in on my stomach and my face. And if I think I look soft, I just assume everyone else is going to see me as sloppy. Or weak. So... yeah. It has a pretty big impact.
Would you say that your concerns about your weight or shape are something that others, like your sister or coworkers, don't seem to understand or think are exaggerated?
I guess... I don't know. I don't really talk to my coworkers about it. And my sister... she hasn't said much. I don't really know what they think.
Do you ever fast for extended periods, severely restrict calories to a minimal amount, or avoid eating entirely for a day or more to manage your weight?

I wouldn't call it fasting. I just... I keep it light. Most days it's just coffee in the morning. If I'm driving between sales calls, maybe I'll have a protein bar. And then dinner is... you know, something small. Like some grilled chicken, no rice or anything. If I sit down and eat a whole meal, it just... it feels like I've ruined the whole day. So I just keep it minimal.
Do you have strict rules about what or when you're allowed to eat, or avoid certain types of food completely because of concerns about your weight or shape?

I mean... I don't know if I'd call them strict rules. I just... I know what works for me and what doesn't. Like I said, I keep it light. I don't really eat carbs or sugar... they just make you feel heavy. I just stick to what I know is safe.
Have you ever taken any specific actions, like exercising more, skipping meals, or avoiding certain foods entirely, specifically to make up for eating more than you planned?

I guess... yeah. Sometimes. Like if I have to take a client out to dinner, or... I don't know, if I go out for a weekend in Miami. If I come back and the scale is even a pound higher, I just... I get this panic. It feels like I'm losing control. So I just... I figure out how to cut back the next day to fix it.
Would you say that your current weight is lower than you originally wanted it to be?
I don't... I don't really know. I haven't really thought about a specific number. I just... I just want to feel okay.
Would you say that your weight loss was something you directly aimed for and worked to achieve, or did it happen without you specifically trying to lose weight?
I don't really know. I wasn't... I didn't have some specific goal to lose weight. I just started paying more attention to things, and... it just sort of happened.
Would you say that your weight or body shape influences how you judge yourself as a person, like whether you feel good or bad about who you are?

I mean... yeah, I guess. It's just... if I'm looking in the mirror before a client meeting, or... or a date... I just sort of end up zeroing in on my stomach. And my face. 

If I think I look... soft... I don't know, I just feel like everyone is going to look at me and think I'm sloppy. Or weak. So... yeah, it bothers me.
When you eat more than you planned, do you ever take specific steps—like exercising longer, skipping meals, or severely restricting food afterward—to make up for it?

I don't... I don't really do that. I mean, I don't plan out my meals like that, so... there's not really a time where I eat more than I planned. I just... I just eat what I need to. So, no, I don't do those things.
Would you say that your weight or body shape influences how you judge yourself as a person, like whether you feel good or bad about who you are?
I... didn't you just ask me that? I thought I already answered it. I mean, yeah, I guess it does. I don't know what else to say about it.
